title: The Yorkshire Ripper Murders
evidence: Physical evidence linked Sutcliffe to multiple attacks
Police investigation connected him to thirteen murders and several attempted murders
Sutcliffe made admissions concerning the killings
Multiple psychiatrists examined him and diagnosed paranoid schizophrenia
modus_operandi: Sutcliffe attacked women, frequently approaching victims in public places before striking them with weapons. He used hammers, knives, and other weapons and repeatedly attacked women over a period of several years.
personality_disorder: Paranoid schizophrenia was diagnosed by multiple psychiatrists during the 1981 trial and subsequently confirmed during his psychiatric treatment. This is a psychotic disorder rather than a personality disorder. The trial jury nevertheless rejected his diminished-responsibility defense and convicted him of murder.
summary: British serial killer responsible for murdering thirteen women and attempting to murder several others. Unlike many serial-killer cases characterized primarily by antisocial or psychopathic traits, Sutcliffe's case involved documented severe psychotic illness, with multiple psychiatrists diagnosing paranoid schizophrenia.
